seeds.name: Group-by summary statistics on a unique id column
seeds.description: 2,000-row lean CSV grouped by its unique id column (2,000 groups); csvtk's summary verb pays a per-group statistics call for each group, about 30-150ms. The block is not repeated (repetition would collide ids and break the unique-key grouping this workload measures), so it is stored in full rather than compactly, but is small enough (2,000 rows, ~26KB) to inline directly.

seeds.name: Multi-key sort of a large employee table
seeds.description: A 2,000-row block repeated 25 times (50,000 rows) sorted on three keys (numeric descending, natural, numeric ascending); about 35-140ms of comparison and record-reordering work. Sort does not care about row uniqueness, so the repeated block measures the same comparison/reordering path as a genuinely distinct 50,000-row table.

seeds.description: Inner join of a 50,000-row employee CSV (a 2,000-row block repeated 25 times) against an 8-row department lookup on the department code; about 35-40ms, exercising csvtk's hash-join path. The join key is the low-cardinality department code, not the employee id, so the repeated block does not change what is measured.

seeds.name: Regex-derived column over a large employee table
seeds.description: A 2,000-row block repeated 25 times (50,000 rows) with a new column derived by regexp capture from an existing column; about 70-135ms, exercising mutate's per-field regex-and-rewrite path, which is row-independent and unaffected by the repeated block.

seeds.name: Composite-key frequency count
seeds.description: A 3,000-row block, each row a distinct (id,dept,val) triple, repeated 10 times (30,000 rows); freq counts 3,000 distinct composite keys at 10 occurrences each rather than 30,000 singleton keys, so the key space is narrower than an equivalent fully-unique table would give, but the same freq/hashing hot path is exercised over the same row volume; about 55-135ms.

seeds.name: Group-by summary statistics at stress scale
seeds.description: 45,000-row lean CSV grouped by its unique id column (45,000 groups), the same operation as employee-summary-by-id scaled up for profiling; about 3.0-4.0s. csvtk's summary verb pays cost per distinct group rather than per row, and does not accept repeated positional file arguments the way seqkit and miller do, so unlike this manifest's other stress seed this one cannot be compressed with stdin_repeat without shrinking the group count and losing the timing target; the block (~653KB) is stored in full rather than compactly, which is why this manifest, unlike the other two, stays above the ~500KB target.
